title: Henselian normalization equals the chosen normalization localization and detects its stabilizer
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and let $\Omega/K$ be an algebraic field extension. Let $B\subset\Omega$ be the integral closure of $A$, i.e. the roots of monic polynomials over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and let $\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $B$ above $\mathfrak m$. Put $T=B_{\mathfrak q}\subset\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and assume that $T$ is a normal henselian local domain [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with fraction field $\Omega$. Let $H$ be a henselization of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], embedded as an $A$-subalgebra of $T$ by a local map. Assume $H$ is a domain and $\Omega/\operatorname{Frac}(H)$ is algebraic. Let $C\subset\Omega$ be the integral closure of $H$. Then $C$ is henselian local, $C=T$, and its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ satisfies $B\cap\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q$. If $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$, then, as subgroups of $G$,
$$ \{\sigma\in G:\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q\}=\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{Frac}(H)}(\Omega). $$

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, decomposition-group comparison; direct normalization argument using more-algebra.tex Tag 092X, lemma-integral-over-henselian.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], $C$ is a subring of the field $\Omega$, contains $H$, and is integral over $H$. In particular it is a nonzero domain. If $e^2=e$ in $C$, then $e(e-1)=0$, so $e=0$ or $1$. Apply [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence] to $H\to C$: $H$ is henselian local by [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], and all the other hypotheses have just been checked. Thus $C$ is henselian local; write $\mathfrak n$ for its unique maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 092X, lemma-integral-over-henselian, domain case; existing connected-integral permanence node specialized to the domain C.

proof.text: One has $B\subseteq C\subseteq T$ inside $\Omega$. Indeed a monic polynomial over $A$ witnessing $b\in B$ is also a monic polynomial over $H$, giving $b\in C$. Conversely, for $c\in C$ its monic equation over $H\subseteq T$ makes it integral over $T$. Since $c\in\Omega=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ and $T$ is normal, [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $c\in T$. These are direct applications of the monic-equation definition [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Tag 0309, definition-domain-normal, and Tags 00GI/00GP, integral elements and integral closure.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m_T$ be the maximal ideal of $T=B_{\mathfrak q}$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak m_T=\mathfrak qT$ and $B\cap\mathfrak m_T=\mathfrak q$: if $b/1\in\mathfrak qT$, putting the finite sum of fractions over a common denominator $s\notin\mathfrak q$ gives $sb\in\mathfrak q$, hence $b\in\mathfrak q$ by primality; the other inclusion is immediate. Now $C\cap\mathfrak m_T$ is a proper ideal of the local ring $C$, so is contained in $\mathfrak n$. Thus $\mathfrak q\subseteq B\cap\mathfrak n$. The latter is a proper ideal of $B$, so maximality of $\mathfrak q$ gives $B\cap\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization; Section 07BH, local rings and the paragraph defining the local ring R_p with maximal ideal pR_p. The ideal inclusions are the elementary argument written here.

proof.text: For $s\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, the equality $B\cap\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q$ says $s\notin\mathfrak n$, so $s$ is a unit in $C$. Every element $b/s$ of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] therefore belongs to $C$: the inverse of $s$ in the subring $C\subseteq\Omega$ is its field inverse. This gives $T\subseteq C$, and step 2 gives the reverse inclusion. Hence $C=T$ as subrings of $\Omega$, with $C$ henselian local and $B\cap\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q$ as already proved.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization, fraction description; Section 07BH, units outside the unique maximal ideal. Direct normalization comparison.

proof.text: Every $\sigma\in G$ preserves $B$: applying $\sigma$ to a monic equation over $A\subseteq K$ gives the same equation for $\sigma(b)$, and applying $\sigma^{-1}$ gives equality. If $\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q$, the formula $b/s\mapsto\sigma(b)/\sigma(s)$ defines an $A$-automorphism of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; it is local because an automorphism preserves units and hence the unique maximal ideal. Its composite with the given local embedding $i:H\to T$ and $i$ itself are local $A$-maps into the henselian local ring $T$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] implies $\sigma\circ i=i$. Thus $\sigma$ fixes $H$ pointwise, and fixes every fraction $h_1/h_2$ with $h_2\ne0$. This proves $\{\sigma:\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q\}\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{Frac}(H)}(\Omega)$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, decomposition-group comparison; ordinary henselization uniqueness as in algebra.tex Tag 04GS, lemma-henselian-functorial, and Tag 08HR, lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit. Explicit fraction action and direct universal-property argument.

proof.text: Conversely, if $\sigma\in G$ fixes $\operatorname{Frac}(H)$, it fixes $H$. Applying $\sigma$ and $\sigma^{-1}$ to monic equations over $H$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] gives $\sigma(C)=C$. Since $C=T$ is local, this automorphism preserves its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. It also preserves $B$ by step 5, so $\sigma(\mathfrak q)=\sigma(B\cap\mathfrak n)=B\cap\mathfrak n=\mathfrak q$. This is the reverse subgroup inclusion and proves the asserted equality inside $G$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia, decomposition-group comparison; direct reverse inclusion using the integral closure and its unique maximal ideal.

Step 1: C⊂Ω is a nonzero domain integral over the henselian H, so it has only the idempotents 0 and 1. This is exactly the hypothesis of lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence (Stacks 092X), and the step uses only that node's stated conclusion that C is henselian local. Step 2: B⊆C⊆T because T is a normal domain with fraction field Ω. Step 3: B∩qT=q since T is a domain, and C∩m_T⊆𝔫; maximality of q, which is a hypothesis, then gives B∩𝔫=q. Step 4: elements of B outside q are units of C, so T⊆C and C=T. Step 5: σ with σq=q restricts to a local A-automorphism of T. The uniqueness clause of def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime gives σ∘i=i, so σ fixes Frac(H); this matches the uniqueness argument in the proof of Stacks 0BSW lemma-identify-inertia (pione.tex:2883). Step 6: if σ fixes Frac(H), it preserves C=T, its maximal ideal 𝔫 and B, so σq=q. Edge cases checked: A a field, Ω=K, and Ω/K purely inseparable or infinite (no step uses separability or finiteness).
